name: nitroso_radical_cucurbituril_anion_rotaxane_imscription

phase_0.boundary_condition: The suprastructural enclosure of the cucurbituril host around the threaded axle, defining the mechanical bond domain.

VINIT.justification: The system before self-assembly, in which the nitroso radical, cucurbituril, and axle fragments exist as separate, unorganized entities with no mechanical bond.

TANCH.justification: The rigid, barrel-shaped cavity provides the closed containment boundary for the radical anion rotaxane, fixing the spatial domain of the assembly.

AFWD.justification: Directed passage of the axle through the cucurbituril cavity toward the final interlocked structure, representing a forward morphism toward the thermodynamically stable rotaxane.

AREV.justification: Reverse transformation in which the axle exits the macrocycle, returning the system to separated components; the descent from the interlocked state.

CLINK.justification: Sequential chaining of the host guest complex formation followed by radical anion generation, the two step composition yielding the target rotaxane.

IMSCRIB.justification: The persistent radical anion species within the cucurbituril cavity maintains its chemical identity via EPR spectral signature, a self referential marker of the interlocked state.

FSPLIT.justification: The neutral nitroso axle upon entering the cucurbituril cavity either accepts an electron (forming the persistent radical anion) or remains in its closed shell diamagnetic state; the two branches diverge at the reduction potential.

FFUSE.justification: If the radical anion branch and the neutral branch of the nitroso axle are reversed back through the same reduction gate, the original neutral nitroso axle preceding the split is recovered exactly, fulfilling the Frobenius condition.

EVALT.justification: Affirmative branch of the reduction gate: the axle accepts the electron, generating the persistent nitroso radical anion inside the cucurbituril cavity.

EVALF.justification: Negative branch of the reduction gate: the axle fails to accept the electron and remains as the neutral, diamagnetic nitroso compound within the cavity.

ENGAGR.justification: A paradice in which the cucurbituril hosted nitroso species exists simultaneously as an open shell radical anion and a closed shell charge transfer complex, the two electronic configurations held without resolution on the EPR timescale.

IFIX.justification: The permanent, irreversible recording of the radical anion signature via electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy, an append only measurement that fixes the radical state in the experimental narrative.

phase_2.split_input: neutral nitroso axle inside cucurbituril cavity
phase_2.fuse_result: neutral nitroso axle inside cucurbituril cavity

phase_3.void_description: The unassembled precursor molecules in solution, prior to any host guest complex formation or electron transfer.
phase_3.true_description: The radical anion state of the nitroso axle threaded inside the cucurbituril cavity, confirmed by a characteristic EPR signal.
phase_3.false_description: The neutral closed shell nitroso axle inside the cucurbituril cavity, producing no EPR response.
phase_3.both_description: The valence tautomeric state where the cucurbituril hosted species fluctuates between radical anion and charge transfer complex faster than the spectroscopic detection window, yielding a time averaged signal that encodes both electronic configurations.

steps.domain_action: dispersed molecular precursors exist as separate, unorganized entities before self-assembly.
the cucurbituril host macrocycle defines the closed spatial boundary that will contain the mechanical bond.
threading assembly proceeds as the axle passes through the cucurbituril cavity toward the interlocked structure.
the preorganized host guest complex forms first, sequentially followed by electron transfer to the bound axle.
the one electron reduction gate splits the neutral nitroso axle state into two potential branches based on electron acceptance.
the radical anion formation branch is activated, producing a persistent open shell species inside the cavitand.
the nitroso radical anion self recognizes its persistent chemical identity through its unique EPR hyperfine coupling pattern.
a valence tautomeric superposition emerges where the radical anion and a charge transfer complex coexist, held without resolution.
the EPR spectral record is written, irreversibly fixing the experimental signature of the radical anion state.
radical anion recombination fidelity operates, converting the radical anion back to the diamagnetic closed shell form if reversed through the gate.
the closed shell retention branch is traversed upon failure of electron transfer, returning the neutral axle.
dethreading dissociation occurs as the neutral axle exits the macrocycle, reversing the interlocking and returning to separate components.

phase_5.compiler_frontend: The electrochemical potential gradient translates the operator's intention to reduce the axle into a controlled electron transfer event.
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: Through space electron tunneling between the electrode and the cucurbituril hosted axle, mediated by the noncovalent host guest interface.
phase_5.memory_mechanism: The relative population of radical anion and closed shell states stored as the spin density distribution within the cucurbituril cavity.
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: The order of operations is determined by the stepwise supramolecular assembly protocol: mixing hosts and guests, equilibration, then application of reductive potential.
phase_5.alfs_store: The canonical reference for this system is the X band continuous wave EPR spectrum of the isolated nitroso radical cucurbituril anion rotaxane recorded in frozen solution at 77 K.

phase_6.cycle_cost: One electron equivalent of electrochemical work per threading reduction cycle.
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: High translational and conformational entropy of the free axle and empty cucurbituril in solution.
phase_6.post_cycle_state: Lower configurational entropy of the interlocked rotaxane compensated by the enthalpic gain of radical anion stabilization within the cavitand.
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — the loss of axle translational freedom upon threading is balanced by solvent reorganization and the entropic gain from releasing counterions at the electrode; the cycle is entropy conservative.
